videos.title: The Pound for Pound Podcast Episode 9: Zahari Zahariev, Lightweight World Champion
videos.summary:
Pound for Pound Podcast Episode 9: Ryan Bowen sits down with Bulgaria's Zahari Zahariev, Lightweight World Champion, multiple-time Bulgarian National Champion and Eliza Cup elite contender.

We talk about how Zahari got into armwrestling, the technique and training behind his world title, competing at the top of the lightweight classes, and where he's heading next.

Stefani Decheva, a world champion in her own right, joined Zahari to translate, and Zahari also took questions from the live chat. Thanks to everyone who sent one in.

videos.title: Back Pressure Gets You to the Fight. Side Pressure Finishes It.
videos.summary:
Back pressure, side pressure, wrist flexion and pronation. Four movements sit at the foundation of everything we do on the table, and once you understand what each one gives you and what it takes away from your opponent, the whole match starts to make sense.

In this video I break down why back pressure decides the level you belong at while side pressure decides who actually finishes, what your hand is really doing when you curl or pronate, why a stable hand is the key to going sideways, and how to build a game plan around a stronger opponent: meet them head on, or take the fight 90 degrees somewhere else.

0:00 The four fundamentals of armwrestling
0:28 Back pressure qualifies you for your level
0:57 Keeping your hand at the centre of the table
1:17 Superior back pressure turns off side pressure
1:39 Height, access and derailing your opponent
2:02 Why the effect shrinks against elites
2:18 Back pressure brings you to the fight, side pressure finishes it
2:30 Side pressure is the vector that finishes every match
3:02 Adding the hand
3:28 Wrist flexion vs back pressure, pronation vs side pressure
3:58 What pronation does to your opponent
4:24 Putting the map together
4:48 Strong, static, neutral pronation
5:14 Stability in your hand and wrist
6:02 Make their hand uncertain
6:29 Training side pressure from the worst hand position
7:13 Why the finish often needs a flop press
7:22 Always remember where you start
7:52 The hand amplifies, it doesn't win
8:09 Building a strategy around the four fundamentals
8:38 Hard counter vs soft counter
9:09 Analyse strengths and weaknesses
9:29 Head on or 90 degrees
9:34 A sport that is alive
10:22 The lifelong study of this sport

videos.title: The Pound for Pound Podcast Episode 8: Cvetan Gashevski, 6x World Champion
videos.summary:
Pound for Pound Podcast Episode 8: Ryan Bowen sits down with Bulgarian legend Cvetan Gashevski, 6x World Champion, 10x European Champion and master technician, universally considered one of the greatest pound for pound armwrestlers of all time.

Cvetan is fresh off winning the World Series of Armwrestling after a 10-minute final with Vrez Sedrakyan. We talk about his start in 1990, his first world and European medals in 1994, how elbow problems turned him into the best defensive top roller in the world, a week of training with Bob Brown, his six-days-a-week table time, his eight-minute war in Japan, Ryan's own exhausting match against him in India, what makes Team Mali so strong, his son's silver medal at the Junior Worlds, and why tiny Bulgaria keeps producing world-class armwrestlers.
